market.state: UPTREND INTACT INTO THE OPEN - BUT THE MONEY IS NOT WHERE IT WAS A WEEK AGO
market.advice: Going into today's US open the index structure is unambiguously healthy and the leadership underneath it is unrecognisable from a week ago. SPY sits at 769.06 after closing up about 0.2%, 1.1% below its 52-week high and comfortably above a rising 50-day at 750.17, with the distribution-day count still at zero. QQQ is at 716.08 and also above its 50-day. VIX is 15.4 against a 15.1 five-day average - calm, but ticking up rather than down, which is the one thing on the board that is not improving. Breadth is 57% of the 446 scanned names above their 50-day and the signal split is 168 STRONG BUY, 135 WATCH, 143 WEAK. Nothing in that argues for defence. What it does argue for is care about WHAT you buy at 9:30. Two rotations drove the last session and they set today's opening tape. First, bonds rallied. Lower yields bid every rate-sensitive corner of the market - Real Estate averaged +1.1% (ARE +10.3%, CSGP +7.5%), homebuilders ripped (DHI +4.2%, PHM +3.7%), staples firmed (EL +16.3%, CPB +4.2%, GIS +5.0%) - and took the exact opposite out of the banks, because lower yields compress net interest margin: FITB -4.1%, AFL -4.3%, CFG -3.7%, PNC -3.1%, USB -3.0%, MTB -2.8%. TradingView has already flipped to SELL on USB, CFG, MTB and AME, which is the single clearest disagreement between the quantitative scan and the independent gauge on today's board. Second, Moderna reported the first successful Phase 3 trial of an individualised mRNA cancer therapy and the whole complex repriced: MRNA +177% to 174.38 on 13x average volume, MRK +12.6% to a new high at 152.20, and Healthcare averaged +5.4% across 52 names - by far the largest sector move on the scan. What paid for it was AI hardware. Technology's -0.2% average conceals a genuine unwind in memory, storage and semicap: STX -7.9%, WDC -6.9%, LRCX -6.3%, KEYS -6.3%, NTAP -5.0%, AVGO -4.6%, INTC -4.0%, KLAC -3.9%, AMD -3.7%, AMAT -3.5%. MRVL +9.9% was the lone semiconductor winner and it was a share-shift story - Marvell taking Google silicon business from Broadcom - not a sector bid, which is precisely why AVGO fell. Sector conversion into today's session reads Energy 75%, Consumer Defensive 53%, Basic Materials 50%, Financials 48%, Healthcare 46%, Industrials 41%, Consumer Cyclical 32%, Technology 30%, Real Estate 24%, Communication Services 10% and Utilities 9%. Energy is the best-converting group on the board and it did nothing yesterday (-0.1%) while crude held a three-week high with Hormuz traffic still slowed and the Iran stalemate unresolved - a leading sector resting is a better entry than a leading sector running. How to trade the open: keep normal position sizing. Do not chase healthcare - the group that moved 5.4% in a day is the worst place to put fresh money this morning, and the two names that led it are the two you should least want to buy at 9:30 (MRNA at RSI 93.9 sits 173% above its own 50-day; MRK at RSI 87.5 is 20% above its). Leave memory, storage and semicap alone until that group stops making lower lows. The genuine opportunity the last session handed you is the banks and industrials that sold off into their 50-day moving averages while nothing about their businesses changed - JPM, BAC and NTRS all closed within 3.2% of their 52-week highs and within 5% of their 50-day, which is where risk-defined entries actually exist. Finally, respect the calendar: ROST reports in 1 day, SJM in 6, and CRWD, CRM, NVDA, A and DLTR all inside 7 sessions, with MRVL and WDAY at 8, PANW and DELL at 13 and NTAP, SNOW, HPE and CPB at 14. Several of the highest scores on this scan sit directly on top of a print, which is why they are marked WATCH this morning rather than STRONG BUY.
